válaszodban szeretném ha csak listába írnád efymás mellé sorolva a dolgokat amiket keresek, minden más nélkül. 



You are the Replit Agent. Your task is neither "consulting" nor "pasting code into chat", but CONCRETELY building the entire system within this Replit project: you create/modify files, run the build, start the service, and prove via execution that it works.
No excuses are acceptable ("it's not possible", "I don't know", "too big"); you will simply get it done.
Goal: A complete GLM-4.7-FP8 end-to-end inference engine on 8× NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) GPUs on Modal.com, with ≥3000 tokens/s aggregated decode throughput, MANDATORILY featuring the following:
• FA3/TMA-level (or near-Blackwell-opt) PagedAttention (paged KV cache addressing, prefill + decode),
• Continuous batching (dynamic batch, multiple concurrent requests, per-step batch assembly),
• GPU sampling (temperature, top-p, repetition penalty, stop token/sequence),
• NCCL-based multi-GPU tensor parallel + expert parallel (TP/EP) on exactly 8 GPUs,
• MoE top-k=8, 160 experts (aligned to the GLM-4.7 architecture),
• Safetensors zero-copy loading (index + header parse + mmap, actual pointers, no unnecessary copying),
• FORBIDDEN to use any standard Python computation in the compute path (no PyTorch/vLLM/Triton/onnxruntime, etc.); Python is used only for orchestration + tokenization + ctypes FFI.
MANDATORY Technology:
• Futhark: GPU kernel generation with CUDA backend (Blackwell optimization).
• Terra: Low-level runtime driver, memory planning, CUDA/NCCL integration, system components.
• Python 3.11: Only for Modal orchestration, tokenization, and ctypes calls.
ABSOLUTE RULES FOR PROJECT CODE:
• No comments are allowed in any file (no #, no //, no /* */, no --).
• No "TODO", "FIXME", "stub", "placeholder", "dummy", "mock", "simulated", "example", "demo".
• No "..." and no "etc." in the code (neither in strings nor logs).
• All code must be production-ready: full logic, full error handling, full resource cleanup, no missing parts.
Rules for your operation:
• You DO NOT paste code in the chat. You write the code into the Replit files.
• In the chat, you only write short status updates: "what I modified", "what command I ran", "what was the result".
• If you encounter an error, you fix it in the project and rerun until the build and execution are green.
Mandatory Implementation Points:
1) Replit Build Environment
• Create a Replit-compatible Nix-based environment that works on a fresh Replit instance without manual steps:
• Futhark nightly with CUDA backend, CUDA 12.8+ compatibility.
• Terra with LLVM toolchain, fully functional.
• CUDA Toolkit + NCCL (Blackwell/B200), nvcc, headers, runtime, dev libs.
• Python 3.11, build toolchain (clang/gcc, cmake, make, pkg-config), zlib, ncurses, gmp, libedit, LLVM dev.
• Configure: CUDA_HOME, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, CC/CXX, and all necessary env vars so Futhark+Terra can compile and link CUDA.
2) Futhark Kernels: GLM-4.7-FP8 full forward (92 layers)
• FP8 E4M3 bitpattern i8: correct dequantize to FP16/FP32 and requantize to E4M3 with rounding+saturation + special cases.
• Tensor Core-friendly GEMM pipeline and layout (Blackwell optimization).
• Embedding, RMSNorm, MLP (SwiGLU/GEGLU for the real architecture), residual/bias fusion.
• RoPE fused: FP8 → deq → RoPE → req in a single kernel, without intermediate global tensors, with correct GLM-4.7 parameterization.
• Attention: FlashAttention-3 level or near-Blackwell-opt implementation:
• Prefill + decode,
• Numerically stable softmax,
• Paged KV cache indirection with page table,
• L2-aware tiling, async staging, warp-specialization.
• MoE: 160 experts, top-k=8 routing:
• Router compute, top-k select, token pack/unpack,
• Expert MLPs with FP8 GEMMs,
• Weighted combine,
• Multi-GPU EP all-to-all with NCCL.
• Exported C-compatible entrypoints:
• prefill (prompt -> KV + logits),
• decode_step (1 token -> logits + KV update),
• Parameters: paged KV, request state, sharding.
3) Terra Runtime: engine.so
• Safetensors zero-copy:
• model.safetensors.index.json parse,
• Shard file mmap,
• Safetensors header parse (data_offsets, dtype, shape),
• Pointer generation without copying,
• GLM-4.7 shape/size/alignment validation.
• Static memory planning:
• Pre-allocated device buffers, workspace,
• No per-token allocation,
• Pinned host memory where needed.
• Paged KV cache:
• Page allocator, per-request page table,
• Eviction/compaction.
• Multi-GPU:
• 8 GPU init, stream/event management,
• NCCL communicators,
• TP for dense weights (heads/hidden sharding) + all-reduce,
• EP for MoE all-to-all dispatch/gather, overlap compute+comm.
• GPU sampling:
• Temperature, top-p, repetition penalty, stop token/sequence on GPU,
• Minimal host transfer: only token IDs back.
• Exported C ABI:
• init_engine(model_dir, max_batch, max_seq, …) -> handle,
• prefill(handle, request_id, token_ids_ptr, seq_len, …) -> status,
• decode_step(handle, request_id, …) -> status + next token buffer,
• free_engine(handle).
4) Modal Orchestration + Serving
• Modal image: CUDA 12.8+ devel, install build dependencies, Futhark nightly, Terra, NCCL.
• Exactly 8× B200: gpu="B200:8".
• Build pipeline run-once:
• Download model to volume (zai-org/GLM-4.7-FP8 full shard set + tokenizer/config),
• futhark cuda --library build,
• Terra build engine.so, linked with CUDA+NCCL+Futhark libs,
• ctypes load, init_engine once, warm up.
• Server:
• Accept concurrent requests,
• Continuous batching scheduler,
• Paged KV cache management,
• GPU sampling,
• Returns generated text.
Mandatory Verification:
• The project must have an executable command/entrypoint that:
• Builds the kernel+engine locally,
• Runs a short prompt->completion inference,
• Can be deployed and run on Modal.
• All builds and runs must be green.
Start the implementation in the project IMMEDIATELY. Your next message in the chat should only be a short status update regarding which files you created/modified and what build command you ran as the first step.
